text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- An anonymous caller told the newspaper Biznes & Baltiya on Wednesday that he would kill the chairman of the Democratic Party Saimnieks, Ziedonis Chevers, within 24 hours. The newspaper informed the security police and security services who are responsible for protecting parliamentary deputies.
- Parliament confirmed the appointment of Olafs Bruvers, the former parliamentary secretary of Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to the post of the director of the Bureau of Human Rights.
- U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbot told President Guntis Ulmanis in The Hague on Wednesday that no country will be left alone in the search for its security policy.
- Parliament approved in the first reading amendments to the constitution to lengthen the terms of office of parliament and the president to four years from three.
- A seminar called oil terminals in Eastern Europe- problems of the environment, will take place in Jurmala on May 30. It will focus on the construction of Lithuania's Butinges oil terminal.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele acknowledged that the political situation is very fragile.
- The Latvian Investment Bank has become the first Latvian bank to issue public bonds. The total value of the bonds is one million lats.
